newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Tenth Indonesian hostage freed in Irian Jaya.
newsitem.headline: Tenth Indonesian hostage freed in Irian Jaya.

text.p: An Indonesian hostage has been freed by kidnappers in the remote province of Irian Jaya, leaving only two of 12 forestry workers originally seized still in captivity, the official Antara news agency said on Monday.

The man was found by troops near the base camp, 60 km (37 miles) east of the mining town of Timika, where the 12 hostages were seized on August 14 while working for PT Kamundan Raya, a unit of diversified timber Djajanti group.
Nine other hostages were released at the end of last month.

The military has said the kidnappers are members of a security disturbing group, a term often used to describe the separatist Free Papua Movement (OPM) whose armed rebels have campaigned against Indonesian rule in the former Dutch colony since 1963.
